subject: history

items.q: Why did Hitler order the Night of the Long Knives in 1934?
items.correct: To eliminate Ernst Röhm and the SA leadership, reassure the army of his authority, and remove rivals — securing the army's loyalty when Hindenburg died weeks later.
items.misconception: Hitler purged the SA because they were Communists.
items.random_wrong: It was a battle in which the SA tried to overthrow Hitler.
items.why: The SA were Nazis, not Communists. Students miss that this was internal consolidation: Hitler traded the SA for army backing, completing the move to total power.

items.q: Which PM led during the Winter of Discontent?
items.why: The answer examiners want is: Callaghan. “Wilson” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: Who was Argentina's president during the Falklands War?
items.why: Correct answer: Galtieri. “Peron” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: In what year was the Big Bang deregulation?
items.why: The real figure is 1986 AD. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
